Pre-registered 2026-08-25 21:20, BEFORE any arm-B checkpoint was evaluated.
Arm A is already known (it is the baseline, not the test) and is quoted below so
the comparison is fully specified in advance.

WHAT IS BEING TESTED
  Does widening the precomputed tempo-augmentation range from -20..+20 to
  -60..+20 improve Beat This on SMC, and is the gain concentrated below 70 BPM
  as the tempo-coverage account predicts?

DESIGN
  Both arms: from scratch, fold 0, 3 seeds, identical corpus (1,954 tracks),
  identical hyperparameters. ONLY difference: tempo range (22 vs 32 precomputed
  variants per track, drawn from ONE shared spectrogram store).
  Neither arm saw ANY SMC track in training, so all 217 are honest test data and
  no fold-honest bookkeeping is needed for the A-vs-B contrast.

ARM A, MEASURED (3 seeds, n=217):
    ALL      0.5818  (sd 0.0095)
    <70      0.5167  (sd 0.0125)   n=103
    70-100   0.6379  (sd 0.0031)   n=76
    >100     0.6460  (sd 0.0186)   n=38

PRIMARY READOUT
  d70 = mean F(arm B) - mean F(arm A) on the 103 tracks below 70 BPM,
  averaged over seeds, paired per track, Wilcoxon over tracks.

DECISION RULE
  PROCEED   d70 >= +0.03  AND  p < 0.01  AND  d70 > d100
            -> the mechanism holds; scale up (folds 5 and 7, then the absolute
               claim against 0.6449 via full-corpus training and/or TTA stacking)
  KILL      d70 <= +0.02
            -> tempo coverage does not fix slow-tempo tracking at this dose.
               The tempo programme ends here. Do NOT re-slice by another band,
               another metric, or another fold to find a win.
  AMBIGUOUS otherwise -> run folds 5 and 7 before interpreting anything.

MECHANISM CHECK (does not override the decision rule, but is reported)
  Arm B's extra data is ENTIRELY slow; there is nothing new above 100 BPM.
  So d70 > d100 is required. A uniform lift across all three bands indicates
  generic regularisation, NOT tempo coverage, and must be reported as such even
  if the headline F improves.

WHAT THIS CANNOT CLAIM
  Absolute performance. Both arms train on ~43% of upstream's data, so neither
  can be compared to the released checkpoints or to the banked TTA 0.6449.
  This experiment measures a DELTA and nothing else.
